title: Mushroom Smash Burgers
changes_from_base: No beef: whole portobello caps brushed with onion-powder oil are pressed flat between two heavy pans until thin and browned, then topped with Cheddar; two caps per bun.
summary: Meaty portobello caps are smashed and melted with tangy Cheddar under a weight until gorgeously caramelised. Fresh lettuce, tomato and classic sauces complete these hefty, satisfying mushroom sandwiches.

ingredients.item: neutral oil (such as rapeseed or grapeseed), plus extra if needed
fine sea salt or table salt
large portobello mushrooms, stalks removed, wiped clean

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Mix 60 ml neutral oil, 1 tsp onion powder, ½ tsp fine salt and ¼ tsp ground black pepper in a small bowl.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Score an X in the top of each of the 4 large portobello mushroom caps and coat all over with the oil mixture.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat one heavy frying pan over medium-high, add the caps and set the foil-wrapped second heavy pan on top; turn every 2 min.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: From about 4 min in, press down on the top pan periodically whilst turning for 8-10 min total until the caps are browned and thin, lowering the heat if they char, adding 1 tbsp more oil if dry.

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Turn heat to low, lay 4 slices of mature Cheddar on top, cover with a lid or tray for 1-2 min until melted.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Put 2 caps in each bun with 2 lettuce leaves, 1 sliced tomato and 4 tsp of mayonnaise, ketchup and/or mustard.

tips: Choose portobello caps of a similar size so they flatten evenly under the pans and are ready at the same time.
Wrap the second pan base in foil to prevent sticking and ensure even heat.
Don't press down before 4 minutes or the delicate flesh will split.
If the mushrooms char too fast, lower the heat slightly.
storage: These are best served immediately, but leftover patties can be refrigerated for up to 2 days and reheated gently under the grill. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
